text_diff: [word/document.xml] Field execution of the rolling backdrop props relies on a coordinated division of responsibility between parent volunteers and student performers:
[word/document.xml] • Trailer Unloading & Staging: Offload backdrop carts from the equipment trailer and roll them to the stadium entrance tunnel or staging chute (Figure 3).

-[word/document.xml] • Ballast Loading & Wind Schedule Compliance: Assess venue wind conditions and stage double-bagged 15-lb sandbags according to the Standardized Tiered Ballasting & Wind Speed Schedule (Section 1.4, Table 1.4). Under Tier 1 normal conditions (0–12 mph), place 2 sandbags over each vertical wing post (4 bags / 60 lbs). Under Tier 2 advisory conditions (12–18 mph), place 3 sandbags over each wing post (6 bags / 90 lbs). Under Tier 3 high-wind conditions (18–22 mph), maintain 3 bags per wing post and place 3 supplemental sandbags flat across the rear 2x4 rail (9 bags / 135 lbs). Never deploy backdrops if sustained winds exceed 20 mph or gusts exceed 25 mph (Tier 4 NO-GO).

+[word/document.xml] • Ballast Loading & Staging: Assess stadium wind conditions and stage double-bagged 15-lb sandbags according to the quick-reference schedule below (see Section 1.4 for full engineering analysis and leverage details):
[word/document.xml] • Pre-Show Safety Check: Verify all four swivel casters rotate freely, brake levers are disengaged for transit, and strut mounting hardware is secure.
[word/document.xml] • Staging Order: Arrange backdrops in numerical show drill order at the field gate.

[word/document.xml] • Exit Catch Crew: Position parent volunteers (holding official Field Pass wristbands per Rule 9.07) at the stadium exit gate to receive carts from students, assist with deceleration, remove ballast sandbags, and pack the trailer.
